extracted.intended_audience: recording artists, producers, engineers, songwriters, music supervisors, record labels and GRAMMY entrants/submission teams
extracted.subtask_description: Screening criteria, eligibility rules, and credit definitions for GRAMMY Award categories, production and engineering credits, and music supervision as used by the Recording Academy for submission and screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer (eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: The producer is the primary person responsible for the creative and technical direction of a recording project; identifies and hires musicians, engineers, singers, arrangers, studios, etc., in collaboration with the artist; assigns credits to performers and technical personnel; and is responsible for supplying accurate crediting information to the record label, media company or content owner as official documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversees staffing needs, keeps budgets and schedules, adheres to deadlines, and supervises mixing, mastering and overall quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-Producer
rubrics_metrics.description: This person generally shares some or all of the producer responsibilities with a producer or another co-producer, and is assigned a co-producer credit by the artist and/or content owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A co-producer makes significant and consequential contributions to the outcome of the production to realize the goals of both the artist and content owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocal Producer / Vocals Produced By (including “Featured Artist” Produced By)
rubrics_metrics.description: This person has overall creative and technical control of the vocal recording on a project and the individual recording sessions that are a part of that project; present in the recording studio or location, working directly with the vocalist(s) and engineer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Makes creative and aesthetic decisions that realize the goals of both the artist and the label in the creation of the vocals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation Producer
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal producer responsible for supervising and/or exercising control over the work assigned to other producers, engineers and others on the project for a compilation soundtrack or historical album.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Has the primary creative responsibility for the selection of music tracks and other components on a compilation soundtrack or historical album. (This credit is eligible in Best Compilation Soundtrack For Visual Media and Best Historical Album Categories only.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersive Audio Producer
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as producer, but for an immersive audio recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Producer (non-eligible producer credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Often a label representative or a person who secures funding for a project; may be responsible for the overall concept and may monitor the project from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically not eligible as a producer credit for GRAMMY purposes because role may be more executive/A&R/funding rather than directly involved in day-to-day production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Producer / Associate Producer / Additional Production (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Person delegated some area of responsibility on a project but reports to the producer or co-producer(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegated, subordinate roles are not eligible for a producer credit in GRAMMY crediting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strings (or Any Other Instrument) Produced By (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Person who works with the individual instruments/elements of the recording and not the overall production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit is not considered equivalent to full producer responsibilities and thus is non-eligible as a producer credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produced on Behalf of (the Content Owner) (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone appointed by the content owner whose job relates more to that of an executive producer and/or A&R; may give overall feedback but is not directly involved in day-to-day tasks of delivering the recording to the content owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a role is treated as non-eligible for producer credit for GRAMMY purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineer (eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: The engineer is the primary person or persons actively responsible for the creative process of recording and/or mixing a project as well as technical issues and decisions; operates (or oversees operation of) equipment during the recording process making creative, technical and aesthetic choices in collaboration with the artist and producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible for realizing the sounds and concepts envisioned for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Engineer / Recorded By
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as engineer, except this person is not involved in final mixing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed By / Mixer / Mix Engineer
rubrics_metrics.description: Person who works directly with the artist, producer and/or content owner making creative decisions to achieve the creative goals of the mix, taking previously recorded tracks and creating a mix-down that can then be mastered and distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remix Engineer / Remixer (Best Remixed Recording Category only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineer/remixer responsible for remixing in the context of the Best Remixed Recording Category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant only for Best Remixed Recording eligibility and criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocals Recorded/Engineered By; “Featured Artist” Recorded/Engineered By
rubrics_metrics.description: An engineer with the same responsibilities as the engineer description above, responsible for the process of recording vocals, including those designated a 'Featured Artist’s' vocals on a project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance Engineer (Classical)
rubrics_metrics.description: An engineer with the same responsibilities as the engineer but most often used in classical music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastering Engineer (role description)
rubrics_metrics.description: An engineer who is the last creative bridge between the mix process and the distribution process; generally works with a final mix and makes final adjustments to the sound before distribution while maintaining the vision of the artist, producer and label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This role prepares the final sonic presentation for distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastering Engineer (statuette eligibility note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastering engineers are not eligible for a GRAMMY statuette except in specific Categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mastering engineers are eligible for a GRAMMY statuette only in the Categories of Best Historical Album; Best Immersive Audio Album; Best Engineered Album, Classical; Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical; Record Of The Year; and Album Of The Year. They are eligible to receive a Winner’s Certificate for all winning genre albums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonmeister (Classical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performs same work as an engineer or balance engineer, but to use the name correctly they must be a graduate of an official Tonmeister program that includes score reading, electronics training, and education in recording, mixing and editing techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration Engineer (Best Historical Album only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for transferring and repairing original flat source tapes and discs, removing or reducing anomalies, unwanted noise or any sound obstructing desirable audio content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal is to take audio from a flawed or compromised recording to one suitable for the mastering engineer to complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersive Audio Engineer
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as engineer, but for a recording created in an immersive audio format; or the engineer who creates a new immersive audio mix of previously recorded material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Tools Engineer / DAW Engineer / Pro Tools Operator (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for operation of a Pro Tools or other Digital Audio Workstation during recording and mix sessions, including archiving and maintenance of recorded material (data files).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not generally called upon to make major aesthetic judgments; not eligible as a credited engineer for GRAMMY statuette purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Tools Editor / DAW Editor (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for operation of a Pro Tools (or other) Digital Audio Workstation during post recording work on musical performances; also responsible for archiving and maintenance of recorded material (data files).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not generally called upon to make aesthetic judgments; non-eligible for engineer credit for GRAMMY statuette purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Pro Tools (or DAW) Engineer (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has same responsibilities as a Pro Tools (or other) digital audio workstation engineer but often worked on a much smaller percentage of a project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation 'Additional' signifies a smaller percentage of contribution; generally non-eligible for primary engineering credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineer for Mix (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Person who organizes and sets up the mix and assists the mix engineer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their creative contribution to the mix would not be considered sufficient to receive a mix engineer credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Engineer / Second Engineer (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for assisting the engineer(s); often keep logs of sessions and materials and operate equipment and have enough skills to step in if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive role; not generally eligible for primary engineer credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Engineer (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the same responsibilities as an engineer but is often given the title 'Additional' to signify that they have worked on a much smaller percentage of a track or project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller-percentage contributors are not considered equivalent to primary engineers for crediting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Mix Engineer / Mix Assistant (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as assistant engineer but only works during the mixing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support role during mixing; not eligible for mix engineer credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix Programming (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Person who programs musical sequencers, samplers and synthesizers in a remix situation where an already finished project is retooled with new musical parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role focused on programming; not equivalent to primary remix engineer for crediting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Editing (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for operating equipment for editing (generally a digital audio workstation); can from time to time be called on to make aesthetic choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editing role is distinct from primary engineering credit; typically non-eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Engineering / Programming (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally a person responsible for the functioning and maintenance of digital recorders and digital audio workstations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical maintenance role; not primary engineer credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: DSD Recording / DSD Engineer / DSD Mixer (non-eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Person responsible for functioning and maintenance of digital recordings using Direct Stream Digital format equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized technical role; not treated as primary engineer credit for statuette eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music Supervisor responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify, secure and supervise any and all music-related talent; liaise and negotiate with talent representation; possess accurate knowledge of all costs associated with delivery of music elements and generate realistic budgets; advise on feasibility of schedule; deliver music elements consistent with technical requirements; manage and/or secure legal rights and clearances; determine viability and securing of ancillary product opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes negotiating Synchronization and Master use licenses, credits, cue sheets, and delivering required elements within scheduling and budgetary parameters; considers promotion and additional revenue streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Of The Year (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings entered should represent the best overall achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements to be considered are the performance, production and engineering; secondary elements include songwriting/composition, arranging and performance of backup vocalists and musicians, as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Album Of The Year (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Albums entered should represent the best overall achievement by the performer(s), album producer(s), engineer(s)/mixer(s), and songwriter(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other elements to be considered are arranging and musicianship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Song Of The Year (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Songs entered should represent the best achievement in songwriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A song must comprise music and lyrics (melody qualifies as music) and must have been released on a recording for the first time, or achieved prominence for the first time, during the current eligibility year. Songs that contain samples or interpolations are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Artist (screening criteria & eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes an artist whose eligibility-year release(s) achieved a breakthrough into the public consciousness and notably impacted the musical landscape; primary element is the artist’s performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum releases to meet eligibility: five singles/tracks or one album. No specified maximum number of releases but Screening Committees determine prior prominence which may disqualify. An artist may not enter this Category more than three times, including as a performing member of an established group. Lists of who is eligible and not eligible (e.g., not eligible: any artist who had achieved a breakthrough in a prior eligibility year; artists with previous GRAMMY nomination as a performer, with exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical (screening criteria & eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in production of non-classical audio recordings for a producer whose body of work released in the eligibility year represents consistently outstanding creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One album OR six tracks/singles constitute the minimum for eligibility; the body of work will be up to nine projects (producer chooses which nine if more submitted). Each producer must provide at least one eligible single or track producing an artist other than themselves. Production teams must enter only projects worked on as a team. Only recordings released in the current eligibility year are eligible; tracks from albums released in a previous year are not eligible. Rereleased, reissued and historical recordings are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical (screening criteria & eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes written excellence in songwriting for songwriters whose body of work released for the first time during the eligibility year represents artistic excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Songwriters must have written a minimum of four songs in which they are credited as a songwriter or co-writer. Songs where the songwriter was also credited as a Primary or Featured Artist or Producer do not qualify to achieve the minimum song threshold. Songwriters may enter up to five more songs in which they have songwriting credits as well as additional credits; maximum number of songs cannot exceed nine. Songs from albums released in a previous year are not eligible; rereleased, covered, remixed, reissued and historical recordings of songs are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Pop Solo Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in a solo vocal or instrumental pop performance with or without accompaniment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Pop Duo/Group Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in a duo, group or collaborative vocal or instrumental pop performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings on which a group receives artist billing are eligible here, even when the vocal features only one member. The entire group or collaborative performance, rather than the presence of a lead vocal performance, determines eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Pop Vocal Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in pop vocal albums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dance/Electronic Recording (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in recordings from established Dance and Electronic genres with production and sensibilities distinctly different from a Pop approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category open to recordings targeted to Dance/Electronic market with significant electronic-based instrumentation generally based around a rhythmic dance beat. Dance remixes are eligible only in Best Remixed Recording. Note: Recording MUST contain greater than 50% new material. If vocals or any significant part of the music were not recorded within last five years or were released prior to this year’s eligibility period, it can only be entered in Best Remixed Recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dance Pop Recording (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dance Pop recognizes generally uptempo, danceable music that follows a pop arrangement, featuring strong rhythmic beats, significant electronic-based instruments with emphasis on vocal performance, melody and hooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dance remixes are eligible only in Best Remixed Recording. Note: Recording MUST contain greater than 50% new material. Vocals are generally present throughout and high in the mix; Dance Pop is eclectic and suitable for a contemporary pop audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dance/Electronic Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in recordings from established Dance and Electronic genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open to recordings targeted to the Dance/Electronic market; albums must be made up of at least 50% Dance/Electronic recordings to qualify. Albums of remixes are not eligible (remixes may be entered in Best Remixed Recording).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Remixed Recording (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in remixed recordings where the remixer takes previously recorded and released material and creatively adds to, alters or transforms it to create a new and unique performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category is not for covers, re-recordings, remastered releases, or edits that are only shortened versions. Addition of a vocal performance without substantive change to the original music recording is not eligible. Singles/tracks do not have to be commercially released for sale or streaming if released to clubs or radio in the U.S. for the first time during the eligibility year. The original recording being remixed does not have to have been released during the current eligibility period. Only the remixed recording needs to be released for the first time during the current eligibility period. Only one version/mix of a recording is eligible in most Categories in any year. Both the remixed version and the original version must be available to the Academy for judging purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Rock Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in a rock performance by a solo artist, collaborating artists, established duo, or established group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Metal Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in a metal performance by a solo artist, collaborating artists, established duo, or established group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Rock Song (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Songs entered should represent the best achievement in songwriting across the spectrum of rock music, including metal; only the merits of the song itself are to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Songs that contain samples or interpolations are eligible. A song must comprise music and lyrics and must have been released on a recording for the first time, or achieved prominence for the first time, during the current eligibility year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Rock Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in albums across the spectrum of rock music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Alternative Music Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in an alternative performance that embraces attributes of progression and innovation in both the music and attitudes associated with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often less intense than rock or more intense than pop; regarded as more original, eclectic or musically challenging; may embrace subgenres or hybrids and performances that do not fit other genre categories. Group-billed recordings are eligible even when the vocal features only one member; entire group performance determines eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Alternative Music Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in alternative music albums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative may be defined as genre-blending, envelope-pushing hybrid mixing jazz, R&B, Hip-Hop, Classical, Experimental, Pop, Rap, Electronic/Dance, Spoken Word etc., and may include contemporary production techniques/instrumentation associated with other genres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best R&B Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in a performance by an R&B solo artist, collaborating artists, established duos, or groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Traditional R&B Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in traditional R&B performance intended for recordings that contain classic R&B/Soul vocal, instrumental and compositional elements distinctly apart from a contemporary approach to the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best R&B Song (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in R&B songwriting that utilizes stylistic intention, song structure, lyrical content, and/or musical presentation to create a sensibility that reflects the broad spectrum of R&B music style and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A song must comprise music and lyrics and must have been released on a recording for the first time, or achieved prominence for the first time, during the eligibility year. Songs that contain samples or interpolations are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Progressive R&B Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in albums of progressive vocal tracks derivative of R&B, intended for artists whose music includes more progressive elements of R&B and may include samples and elements of hip-hop, rap, dance, and electronic music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May incorporate production elements found in pop, Euro-pop, country, rock, folk, and alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best R&B Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in albums of R&B music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Rap Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in a performance by a solo rap artist, collaborating rap artists, established rap duos, or established rap groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Melodic Rap Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in performances that use the delivery of rap and melody over modern production; requires a strong and clear presence of melody combined with rap cadence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusive of dialects, lyrics or performance elements from non-rap genres; production may include traditional rap elements or elements characteristic of other genres. Both the song and melody should be considered to fit these criteria to be accepted in this Category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Rap Song (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in rap music songwriting that utilizes stylistic intention, song structure, lyrical content, and/or musical presentation to reflect the broad spectrum of rap music style and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A song must comprise music and lyrics and must have been released on a recording for the first time, or achieved prominence for the first time, during the current eligibility year. Songs that contain samples or interpolations are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Rap Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in albums of rap music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening criteria specify vocal performances only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Spoken Word Poetry Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in spoken word poetry albums; spoken word is an oral poetic performance art that refers to the poem and the performers' aesthetic qualities such as intonation, vocal inflections, rhythmic cadence, and musicality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Albums with or without music accompaniment are eligible; incidental talk or conversation used as accent to a musical recording does not constitute a spoken word poetry performance. Compilations/excerpts of previously broadcast shows, albums of sound effects, and environmental recordings are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Jazz Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in a performance by a jazz solo artist, collaborating artists, established duos, or groups, with emphasis on jazz improvisation and ensemble interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jazz instrumental and jazz vocal tracks are both eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Jazz Vocal Album (screening criteria & eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in albums by jazz vocal soloists, duos, or groups, and/or large ensembles featuring voice, with attention to differentiating elements of vocal performance/interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vocal elements include improvisational phrasing, melodic-based improvisation, jazz style, and harmonic/melodic vocabulary of jazz. Vocal performances, styling, arrangements, and interpretation must be jazz in content and a tributary of the vocal jazz tradition, and not pop/R&B or other non-jazz genre vocal performances employing some jazz flavoring. If vocalists and instrumentalists are billed equally, both/all may be eligible. An entire album entered in Jazz Vocal may not be entered again in Jazz Instrumental. If vocalist(s) and instrumentalist(s) billed equally, the Academy will determine appropriate Category based on number or playing time of vocal vs instrumental tracks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Jazz Instrumental Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in albums by individuals or groups generally thought of as 'small jazz groups' (typically one to eight musicians) performing jazz music, including straight-ahead and contemporary jazz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include albums with larger back-up ensembles if the essence is a small group performance; extent of interaction between soloist(s) and large ensemble is deciding factor; size alone not determinative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Large Jazz Ensemble Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence on albums of large jazz ensemble performance, primarily recordings with a 'big band sound' or large ensemble orchestrational arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally ensembles must contain nine or more members to be eligible (excluding conductor/bandleader). Recordings that use synthesizers to imitate the sound of a large jazz ensemble are not eligible. Large jazz vocal ensemble albums must be entered in Best Jazz Vocal Album.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Latin Jazz Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in Latin Jazz albums by ensembles of any size or orchestration representing the blending of Jazz and improvisation with Latin and Iberian-American music, Brazilian, and Argentinian tango music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Alternative Jazz Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in Alternative Jazz albums by individuals, duos, groups/ensembles, with or without vocals; Alternative Jazz may be defined as genre-blending, envelope-pushing hybrid mixing jazz with other genres and contemporary production techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrumental albums in the well-established Smooth Jazz style remain in the Contemporary Instrumental Category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album (screening criteria & eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in albums consisting of a type and style of song and/or performance that cannot properly be intermingled with present forms of pop music (e.g., Great American Songbook, classic popular music, musical theatre songs independent of narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings eligible include contemporary pop songs performed in a traditional pop style, theatrical-style songs, benefit/tribute/concert/cabaret albums of such repertoire. Additional eligibility: Albums must contain more than 75% newly recorded (previously unreleased) performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Contemporary Instrumental Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporary instrumental music embraces a variety of musical genres; the album concept and production should emphasize instrumental performance, arrangement and/or melodic content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Music should contain contemporary stylistic elements, setting it apart from well-established instrumental styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Musical Theater Album (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: For recordings of the score of a musical theater work created to support an underlying dramatic intention or theme; honors excellence in the performances and production of musical theater recordings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements of the corresponding stage production should not be considered in evaluating the recording. Recordings of revues that reflect a dramatic theme are eligible. Eligible entries must be recordings of work created to support an underlying dramatic intention or theme. Benefit/tribute concerts and recordings of concert tours are not eligible; non-musical theater performance albums are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Country Solo Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in recordings of country music performances by solo artists (with or without band accompaniment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Country Duo/Group Performance (screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes country music recordings, vocal and instrumental, which utilize stylistic intention, song structure, lyrical content and/or musical presentation to create a sensibility that reflects the broad spectrum of country music style and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent is to recognize country music that remains reminiscent of its culture’s legacy while also engaging contemporary forms that push boundaries but remain relevant in country music culture.
